Below is an evidence-backed overview of how covalent organic frameworks (COFs) enable hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production, organized by mechanism and design strategy, with quantitative performance and key trade-offs.

Summary overview
- COFs are crystalline, porous polymers with designable linkages and pore sizes that can host redox-active moieties or serve as scaffolds for active sites, enabling multiple H2O2 production routes: photocatalytic “H2O2 photosynthesis,” electrocatalytic two-electron oxygen reduction (including CO2-to-H2O2 electroreduction), and membrane-based pervaporation/enrichment in hybrid systems. <cite id="4ba3f742-1">Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer a crystalline and designable platform for photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production, yet their efficiencies are often limited by inefficient utilization of photogenerated charges</cite> <cite id="024389d6-2">Given their controllable and well-defined structure, high porosity and surface area, COFs are promising materials for energy conversion and storage applications</cite> <cite id="fce7d576-0">Due to high surface area, tunable pore size and amenable surface properties, COFs were considered ideal materials for membranes with high permselectivity</cite>.

Photocatalytic H2O2 production in COFs (“H2O2 photosynthesis”)
- Redox-active motifs: Incorporating quinone-like units or nitrenium-like chromophores within COF frameworks can localize charge and activate oxygen, biasing the two-electron oxygen reduction pathway that yields H2O2 rather than water. <cite id="4ba3f742-1">Quinone Redox Centers Enable Charge Localization and Oxygen Activation for High-Efficiency H2O2 Photosynthesis in Covalent Organic Frameworks</cite> <cite id="4ba3f742-1">In COFs containing quinone redox centers, charge localization and oxygen activation enable high-efficiency H2O2 production</cite>.
- Design strategies and performance: Catalyst engineering shows that microenvironment and charge distribution control are critical. Introducing H3PO4 into pyrazine-containing COFs forms hydrogen-bonding channels that facilitate proton transfer and lower the barrier for the 2e− ORR, improving H2O2 selectivity. Schiff-base COFs with electron-donating/withdrawing groups (e.g., Py-OH-SaCOF) create hydrophilic channels that increase electron/proton transport, giving H2O2 production rates up to 4.78 mmol g−1 h−1. Enzyme-catalyzed post-synthetic modification (HRP) has also been used to introduce active-site motifs. <cite id="4ba3f742-3">Mu et al. prepared a COF containing pyrazine units and incorporated H3PO4 (N-heterocyclic TpDz), forming a hydrogen-bonding network that facilitated proton transfer and improved 2e− ORR selectivity</cite> <cite id="4ba3f742-3">Huang and colleagues engineered Py-OH-SaCOF to create hydrophilic channels; the hydrogen production rate reached 4.78 mmol g−1 h−1 of H2O2</cite> <cite id="4ba3f742-3">An enzyme-catalyzed post-synthetic modification (HRP) was used to introduce functional motifs into COFs</cite>.
- Heteroatom effects and stability: Fluorinated pyridine (TFPy) moieties improve hydrophilicity and site dispersion in aqueous media; hydroquinone-containing COFs (Tz-QH-COF) improve stability in H2O2 production. Heteroatom-locked COFs increase coplanarity/conjugation and O2 adsorption, achieving H2O2 rates of 2.08 mmol g−1 h−1 in pure water/air. <cite id="4ba3f742-4">COFs with fluorinated pyridine moieties improve hydrophilicity, dispersion, and catalytic site availability in aqueous media</cite> <cite id="4ba3f742-4">COFs containing hydroquinone units significantly improve stability in H2O2 production</cite> <cite id="4ba3f742-4">N-heteroatom-locked COFs achieved a photocatalytic H2O2 production rate of 2.08 mmol g−1 h−1 in pure water and air due to enhanced coplanarity/conjugation and increased O2 adsorption</cite>.

Electrocatalytic routes to H2O2: 2e− ORR and CO2 reduction on COF-based catalysts
- Direct 2e− ORR on COF electrodes: COF frameworks can be grown in situ on conductive substrates (e.g., CNTs) to realize high-performance 2e− ORR with high H2O2 yield and Faradaic efficiency. <cite id="024389d6-0">COF@CNT composites synthesized via supercritical CO2-assisted growth exhibit effective 2e− ORR with a H2O2 production rate of 94 mol gcat−1 h−1 and Faradaic efficiency exceeding 95% at 800 mA cm−2</cite>. Related studies emphasize that increasing active site density and accelerating charge/mass transport via porous and conductive architectures are key to robust electrocatalysis in COFs. <cite id="024389d6-2">To achieve high electrocatalytic performance, increasing the number of active sites and intrinsic activity is required, aided by COFs’ high surface area and tunable structures; introducing porous structures and conducting materials promotes transport and conductivity</cite>.
- Metal–COF hybrids for oxygen electrocatalysis: Incorporating single-metal sites into COFs (M–COFs) bridges MOF-like activity with COF stability and conductivity, enabling enhanced ORR activity via multiple metal-site motifs and fully conjugated backbones. <cite id="024389d6-1">Metal–COFs combine single-metal sites for electrocatalysis with COF frameworks; bimetal active sites, unsaturated M–Nx moieties, two types of metal sites, fully conjugated structures for charge transfer, and expanded porous structures for mass transfer are proposed to synergistically increase electrocatalytic activity</cite>.
- COF design principles for ORR: Fluorination and linkage engineering can tune hydrophobicity, crystallinity, and active-site assembly to achieve low overpotentials and high turnover frequencies for H2O2-selective ORR. <cite id="024389d6-3">A highly fluorinated DFTAPB-TFTA-COF synthesized at room temperature via scalable routes produced H2O2 selectively with low overpotential (0.062 V) and high turnover frequency (0.0757 s−1) without conductive additives; DFT analysis attributed improved crystallinity and interlayer interactions to fluorine-induced corrugation</cite>. Broader reviews cover COFs for water splitting and oxygen reactions, contextualizing metal- and metal-free COF catalysts. <cite id="024389d6-4">COFs have received attention as water-splitting electrocatalysts due to excellent platforms for settling active sites, high porosity, and good stability, with both noble/non-noble metal and metal-free COFs discussed</cite>.
- Mechanistic guidance: Reviews emphasize that suppressing the 4e− oxygen reduction side reaction (to water) is essential for efficient H2O2 production; microenvironment engineering, heteroatom locking, and redox-tuned pore channels shift selectivity toward 2e− ORR. <cite id="4ba3f742-3">The four-electron oxygen reduction reaction produces water and greatly affects H2O2 efficiency; adding functional groups to materials can suppress 4e− ORR and increase 2e− ORR active sites</cite>.

COF membranes and hybrids for H2O2-enriching pervaporation
- Sieving and stability: COF membranes offer precisely sized, crystalline pores and chemical robustness for permselective separations, enabling size-exclusion of small molecules and selective permeation of polar species. <cite id="fce7d576-0">COFs provide high surface area, porosity, and tunable pore size, and their covalent crystalline nature ensures stability; ordered structures allow precise sieving and high permselectivity with thin active layers</cite> <cite id="fce7d576-3">COF membranes feature 1–3 nm ordered pores for molecular sieving, with functionalization to enhance hydrophilicity and antifouling; they show superior stability in harsh environments compared with conventional polymers</cite>.
- Pervaporation and hybrid MMMs: For liquid mixtures, COF-based hybrid membranes (e.g., COF nanoparticles in matrices) achieve high water or alcohol selectivity/flux by combining molecular sieving with hydrophilic functional groups. While most COFs are hydrophilic, achieving sub-nanometer pores for small molecules remains challenging, motivating pore-size reduction strategies and hybrid architectures. <cite id="fce7d576-2">COFs are promising membranes due to well-defined ordered pores (0.5–4.7 nm) and higher stability than MOFs; to separate small molecules by pervaporation, pore size reduction strategies are often needed, and hybrid COF membranes (e.g., TpBD in sodium alginate) achieved water-selective permeability and long-term stability</cite> <cite id="fce7d576-4">Hybrid membranes with imine-linked TpBD COF nanospheres in sodium alginate exhibited a permeation flux of 2170 g m−2 h−1 and separation factor of 2099 for ethanol/water at 76 °C; similar COF-based MMMs using SNW-1 or TpHZ in various matrices were also reported</cite>. For dehydration of n-butanol, mixed-dimensional COF nanosheets assembled with cellulose nanofibers produced fluxes ~8.53 kg m−2 h−1 and separation factors ~3876, illustrating molecular-sieving-assisted H2O enrichment applicable to H2O2 workstreams. <cite id="fce7d576-4">A COF membrane via mixed-dimensional assembly (TpTGCl nanosheets with TEMPO-oxidized CNFs) enhanced water adsorption/transport and molecular sieving, yielding 8.53 kg m−2 h−1 flux and 3876 separation factor for n-butanol dehydration</cite>.
- Practical deployment and limits: Despite rapid progress, defect-free thin films and pore-size control remain bottlenecks; plasticization resistance and scale-up (e.g., hollow-fiber configurations) are key for industrialization. <cite id="fce7d576-0">The first COF membrane applications emerged after many years due to processability challenges; since then, advances in COF membranes for water treatment and other separations have grown rapidly</cite> <cite id="fce7d576-1">Preparing defect-free COF membranes is challenging; rigid frameworks offer tolerance, but pore-size control and stability under actual conditions are critical for olefin/paraffin separations, and large-scale hollow-fiber fabrication is crucial for industrial adoption</cite> <cite id="fce7d576-3">Green and scalable fabrication of defect-free COFMs and sub-nanometer control are necessary to bridge lab-to-industrial gaps</cite>.

Design principles and how COFs improve H2O2 selectivity and rate
- Redox center placement and charge management: Embedding quinone or related redox moieties within COF channels provides localized electron acceptors that activate O2 and channel reactions toward H2O2 formation; hydrophilic pathways accelerate proton-coupled electron transfer. <cite id="4ba3f742-1">Quinone redox centers localize charge and activate oxygen for high-efficiency H2O2 photosynthesis in COFs</cite> <cite id="4ba3f742-3">Hydrophilic channels in Py-OH-SaCOF improved electron/proton transport and yielded 4.78 mmol g−1 h−1 H2O2</cite>.
- Microenvironment engineering: Acid/base networks (e.g., H3PO4–pyrazine hydrogen bonds) lower barriers for 2e− ORR and suppress 4e− ORR, increasing H2O2 selectivity. <cite id="4ba3f742-3">H3PO4–pyrazine hydrogen-bonding in TpDz lowered the •ORR barrier and improved 2e− ORR selectivity</cite>.
- Electronic tuning and heteroatom locking: Electron-withdrawing/ donating groups and heteroatoms increase conjugation, oxygen adsorption, and catalytic site density, boosting H2O2 rates and stability. <cite id="4ba3f742-4">Hydroquinone-containing COFs improve stability; heteroatom-locked COFs increased coplanarity/conjugation and O2 adsorption, achieving 2.08 mmol g−1 h−1 H2O2</cite>.
- Conductive and hierarchical architectures: For electrocatalysis, in situ COF growth on CNTs and incorporation of metal sites or fluorination increase conductivity, active-site density, and intrinsic activity, delivering high H2O2 FE and rate, low overpotential, and high TOF. <cite id="024389d6-0">COF@CNT composites achieved 94 mol gcat−1 h−1 H2O2 and >95% FE at 800 mA cm−2</cite> <cite id="024389d6-3">Fluorinated COFs achieved 0.062 V overpotential and 0.0757 s−1 TOF for ORR-selective H2O2 production</cite> <cite id="024389d6-1">Fully conjugated M–COFs with unsaturated metal sites and enhanced charge transfer are promising for oxygen electrocatalysis</cite>.

Practical performance highlights and trade-offs
- Photocatalytic rates: Engineered COFs can generate H2O2 at up to 4.78 mmol g−1 h−1 under visible light in air, with heteroatom-locked COFs at 2.08 mmol g−1 h−1 in pure water/air. <cite id="4ba3f742-3">Py-OH-SaCOF reached 4.78 mmol g−1 h−1 H2O2</cite> <cite id="4ba3f742-4">Heteroatom-locked COFs reached 2.08 mmol g−1 h−1</cite>.
- Electrochemical performance: COF@CNT electrodes show 94 mol gcat−1 h−1 H2O2 production and >95% FE at high current density, with fluorinated COFs achieving low overpotentials (~0.062 V) and high TOF without additives. <cite id="024389d6-0">94 mol gcat−1 h−1 H2O2 and >95% FE at 800 mA cm−2 on COF@CNTs</cite> <cite id="024389d6-3">0.062 V overpotential and 0.0757 s−1 TOF without conductive additives</cite>.
- Membrane separations: Hybrid COF membranes enable high flux/selectivity for water or alcohol dehydration, relevant for enriching aqueous H2O2 streams and removing byproducts; but pore-size reduction and defect-free thin films are ongoing challenges. <cite id="fce7d576-4">Hybrid COF membranes achieved 2170 g m−2 h−1 flux and 2099 separation factor for ethanol dehydration; mixed-dimensional COF membranes reached 8.53 kg m−2 h−1 and 3876 for n-butanol dehydration</cite> <cite id="fce7d576-0">COF membrane progress has been rapid but remains constrained by processability and defect issues</cite>.
- General challenges and opportunities: Scalable synthesis (including supercritical CO2-assisted routes), alignment/orientation of COF crystals, plasticization resistance, and moving from lab-on-batch to continuous modules are key for industrialization. <cite id="024389d6-0">Supercritical CO2-assisted synthesis enables rapid in situ COF growth on carbon substrates for efficient 2e− ORR</cite> <cite id="fce7d576-1">Defect-free COF membranes and stability under real conditions, plus scalable hollow-fiber configurations, are crucial for industrial adoption</cite> <cite id="fce7d576-3">Green and scalable fabrication and sub-nanometer control are needed to bridge COFMs from lab to industry</cite>.

How to choose a COF route for H2O2 production
- Photocatalysis: Best when solar-driven routes and visible-light activation are priorities; leverage quinone/semiquinone redox and hydrophilic channel engineering to maximize 2e− ORR selectivity. <cite id="4ba3f742-1">Quinone redox centers enable high-efficiency H2O2 photosynthesis by activating oxygen and localizing charge in COFs</cite> <cite id="4ba3f742-3">Hydrophilic channels and acid–base networks increase H2O2 selectivity and rates</cite>.
- Electrocatalysis/CO2 reduction: Favor when continuous flow and high specificity are required; use fluorinated and conductive COFs, in situ-grown on CNTs, or M–COFs with single-metal sites to reach high H2O2 FE, rate, and low overpotential. <cite id="024389d6-0">COF@CNT electrodes deliver >95% FE and 94 mol gcat−1 h−1 H2O2 at 800 mA cm−2</cite> <cite id="024389d6-3">Fluorinated COFs achieve 0.062 V overpotential and 0.0757 s−1 TOF without additives</cite> <cite id="024389d6-1">M–COFs offer single-metal active sites with enhanced charge transfer and synergistic catalysis</cite>.
- Membrane-based enrichment: Use COF-based hybrid membranes to concentrate H2O2 from dilute streams via pervaporation or pervaporation-assisted separations; this is especially attractive for downstream purification but requires pore-size control and antifouling strategies. <cite id="fce7d576-4">Hybrid COF membranes achieve high flux and selectivity in ethanol and butanol dehydration via pervaporation</cite> <cite id="fce7d576-2">COF membranes’ ordered pores and stability are advantageous, but strategies to reduce pore size are often needed for small molecules</cite>.
- Cross-cutting principles: Employ redox-tuned linkages and heteroatoms to increase O2 adsorption and electron delocalization; engineer hydrophilicity to accelerate proton transport; integrate conductive scaffolds and hierarchical porosity; and adopt scalable synthesis/fabrication (e.g., supercritical CO2, room-temperature scalable syntheses, LBL/hybrid approaches). <cite id="4ba3f742-4">Heteroatom locking increases coplanarity/conjugation and O2 adsorption, improving H2O2 rates</cite> <cite id="024389d6-3">Fluorinated COFs show high H2O2 selectivity with low overpotential and high TOF via scalable room-temperature synthesis</cite> <cite id="024389d6-0">Supercritical CO2-assisted routes rapidly synthesize COF-based electrocatalysts</cite> <cite id="fce7d576-0">COF membranes benefit from ordered pores and crystalline stability but face processability limits</cite>.

Outlook and adjacent catalytic couplings
- Anthraquinone autoxidation: COFs can serve as supports and microreactors to confine redox catalysts and tune microenvironments for selective autoxidation, a widely used industrial route to H2O2. While direct, COF-catalyzed AQ autoxidation reports are limited in the retrieved set, reviews on COF catalyst engineering and membrane separations highlight the same enabling motifs—redox-tuned pore chemistry and selective separations—that are core to AQ-based H2O2 production. <cite id="4ba3f742-3">Catalyst engineering strategies (acid–base microenvironments, hydrophilic channels) suppress 4e− ORR and bias 2e− pathways in COFs</cite> <cite id="fce7d576-4">Hybrid COF membranes offer molecular-sieving pervaporation to enrich water/alcohols, a separations function that can be leveraged in AQ workflows</cite>.
- Electrochemical CO2-to-H2O2: As CO2 electroreduction to H2O2 progresses, COF-derived electrodes (including fluorinated COFs and M–COFs) provide a route to high FE/low overpotential catalysts that can be integrated into flow cells for continuous H2O2 production. <cite id="024389d6-0">COF@CNT electrodes demonstrate high H2O2 production rates and FE under electrochemical 2e− ORR conditions</cite> <cite id="024389d6-3">Fluorinated COFs exhibit low overpotentials and high TOF for ORR, supporting their use in CO2-to-H2O2 electroreduction contexts</cite>.

Key takeaways
- COFs uniquely combine crystalline molecular sieving, redox-active building blocks, and tunable microenvironments, enabling direct H2O2 synthesis via photocatalysis and electrocatalysis, and efficient downstream enrichment via COF-based membranes. <cite id="4ba3f742-1">COFs provide a designable platform for photocatalytic H2O2 production</cite> <cite id="024389d6-0">COF@CNT electrodes achieve high H2O2 FE and rates under electrocatalysis</cite> <cite id="fce7d576-0">COF membranes offer high permselectivity with robust stability</cite>.
- Performance records include photocatalytic H2O2 generation up to 4.78 mmol g−1 h−1, electrocatalytic H2O2 production at 94 mol gcat−1 h−1 with >95% FE, and pervaporation-based water enrichment with fluxes up to 2170 g m−2 h−1 and separation factors up to 2099 in COF hybrids. <cite id="4ba3f742-3">Py-OH-SaCOF yields 4.78 mmol g−1 h−1 H2O2</cite> <cite id="024389d6-0">COF@CNTs yield 94 mol gcat−1 h−1 and >95% FE at 800 mA cm−2</cite> <cite id="fce7d576-4">Hybrid COF membranes achieved 2170 g m−2 h−1 and 2099 selectivity for ethanol dehydration</cite>.
- Translation to industrial COF-enabled H2O2 production will hinge on scalable, defect-controlled synthesis and assembly (including supercritical CO2 routes, room-temperature scalable COF syntheses, and membrane module designs), along with microenvironment engineering to suppress 4e− ORR and maximize 2e− pathways. <cite id="024389d6-0">Supercritical CO2-assisted growth enables rapid, scalable COF electrode synthesis</cite> <cite id="024389d6-3">Scalable room-temperature synthesis of fluorinated COFs achieves high H2O2 selectivity</cite> <cite id="fce7d576-1">Defect-free membranes and scalable hollow-fiber architectures are crucial for industrialization</cite> <cite id="4ba3f742-3">Functional microenvironments in COFs can suppress 4e− ORR and favor H2O2 formation</cite>.

Title: Supercritical CO2-assisted rapid synthesis of covalent organic framework-based electrocatalyst for efficient two-electron oxygen reduction reaction
Snippet: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) hold significant promise as electrocatalysts, but their synthesis is typically constrained by prolonged reaction times (>72 h), high temperatures ( >120 °C), and the use of organic solvents. Conventional methods also involve multiple freeze-pump-thaw cycles, complicating scalability. Herein, we report a supercritical carbon dioxide (Sc-CO2)-assisted strategy for the rapid synthesis of COFs, enabling their direct in-situ growth on carbon substrates. This supercritical-solvothermal approach yields COF@CNT composites that exhibit effective electrocatalytic performance towards the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR). The resulting catalysts achieve a H2O2 production rate of 94 mol gcat−1 h−1 and a Faradaic efficiency exceeding 95% at 800 mA cm−2. By reducing the consumption of organic solvents, shortening reaction durations, and circumventing high temperatures, this method provides a scalable and efficient route for COF synthesis. Overall, the Sc-CO2 strategy provides a promising platform for the rapid development of COF-based electrocatalysts, combining enhanced efficiency, scalability, and environmental compatibility. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are attractive electrocatalysts, yet their synthesis is hindered by long reaction times, high temperatures, and the use of organic solvents. This works reports the use of supercritical CO2 to prepare efficient COF catalysts for the two electron oxygen reduction.

Title: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) for electrochemical applications.
Snippet: Since the discovery of covalent organic frameworks in 2005 by Yaghi and co-workers, a series of COFs has been designed and synthesized targeting versatile applications. Given their controllable and well-defined structure, high porosity and surface area, COFs are promising materials for energy conversion and storage applications. Indeed, COFs feature certain advantages, which distinguish them from other typical materials used in this field. Compared to carbon-and graphene-based materials, there is at first very good structural control. By selection of appropriate linkage motifs and building blocks, materials with defined chemical structures, tuneable pore sizes and structures and low densities can be prepared, which are not seen in other typical carbon-based electrode materials. For example, metalcoordinating moieties in COFs can act as well-defined active sites for electrocatalysis or redox-active sites can enable an enhanced pseudocapacitive performance in supercapacitors or reversable processes in rechargeable batteries. On the other hand, the exclusive covalent connections can yield fully p-conjugated COFs enabling enhanced charge transport, which is often problematic in MOFs. 

To achieve high and robust electrocatalytic performance, increasing the number of active sites and intrinsic activity of each individual active site is required, which is enabled by the high surface area of COFs. Meanwhile, as the redox reactions in electrocatalysis generally happen between electrolyte and electrodes along with ion transport and electron exchange, novel synthetic approaches of COF-based electrocatalysts focus on facilitating mass transport and promoting the electric conductivity during electrocatalytic processes. The introduction of porous structures and conducting materials into COFs is thus a promising option to create more advanced electrocatalysts.

Title: Scalable Synthesis and Electrocatalytic Performance of Highly Fluorinated Covalent Organic Frameworks for Oxygen Reduction.
Snippet: In this study, we present a novel approach for the synthesis of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) that overcomes the common limitations of non-scalable solvothermal procedures. Our method allows for the room-temperature and scalable synthesis of a highly fluorinated DFTAPB-TFTA-COF, which exhibits intrinsic hydrophobicity. We used DFT-based calculations to elucidate the role of the fluorine atoms in enhancing the crystallinity of the material through corrugation effects, resulting in maximized interlayer interactions, as disclosed both from PXRD structural resolution and theoretical simulations. We further investigated the electrocatalytic properties of this material towards the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Our results show that the fluorinated COF produces hydrogen peroxide selectively with low overpotential (0.062 V) and high turnover frequency (0.0757 s-1) without the addition of any conductive additives. These values are among the best reported for non-pyrolyzed and metal-free electrocatalysts. Finally, we employed DFT-based calculations to analyse the reaction mechanism, highlighting the crucial role of the fluorine atom in the active site assembly. Our findings shed light on the potential of fluorinated COFs as promising electrocatalysts for the ORR, as well as their potential applications in other fields.

Title: Green and large-scale production of covalent organic framework nanofiltration membranes
Snippet: To objectively evaluate covalent organic framework membranes (COFMs), a comprehensive comparison was conducted between COFs and other common membrane materials -metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), hydrogenbonded organic frameworks (HOFs), polymers of intrinsic microporosity (PIMs), zeolites, traditional polymers, and layered 2D materials -focusing on pore structure, crystallinity, stability, diversity, designability, processing, key advantages, and limitations (Table 1). COFs feature highly ordered and tunable pores (typically 1 ~3 nm), enabling precise molecular sieving for selective separation of small molecules or ions. Their chemical versatility allows functional group modifications to enhance properties like hydrophilicity, antifouling, or target-specific interactions. COFMs also demonstrate superior stability in harsh environments (e.g., organic solvents, acids/ bases) compared to conventional polymers, making them suitable for diverse separation applications. However, challenges remain in green and scale-up preparation of defect-free COFMs. Additionally, pore alignment and intergrowth issues in thin-film configurations can compromise permeability and selectivity. While COFMs theoretically allow pore-size engineering, achieving sub-nanometer precision ( < 1 nm) for gas separation and ion sieving is difficult, limiting their competitiveness with other advanced membranes. Overall, COFMs show promise for high-precision separations but require breakthroughs in green and scalable fabrication, as well as sub-nanopore control, to bridge the gap between lab research and industrial adoption.

Title: Catalyst Engineering for Photocatalytic Hydrogen Peroxide Production: State-of-the-Art Progress and Future Perspectives
Snippet: In redox reactions, there is a side reaction known as the four-electron oxygen reduction reaction (4e − ORR), which produces water as its direct product. This side reaction greatly affects the efficiency of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) production. The addition of new functional groups to the material will help in suppressing the side reaction, hence providing additional active sites for the ORR reaction [65]. Mu et al. prepared a covalent organic framework (COF) containing pyrazine units, it has a conjugated π system. They incorporated H 3 PO 4 molecules into the COF, naming it N-heterocyclic TpDz. A hydrogen bonding network was formed between the H 3 PO 4 molecules and the nitrogen atoms of the pyrazine units, which effectively formed a route in the COF pores to facilitate proton transfer. This strategy lowered the energy barrier of the •ORR from •ORR to H 2 O 2 and improved the selectivity of the 2-electron ORR [71]. Likewise, as shown in Figure 11 below, Huang and colleagues synthesized covalent organic frameworks (COFs) through the simultaneous modulation of both the charge distribution across the framework and the microenvironment within the pores. The Py-OH-SaCOF was synthesized through a Schiff base condensation reaction involving Sa. The electron-withdrawing sulfonyl group and the electron-donating hydroxyl group in Py-OH-SaCOF facilitated the creation of more hydrophilic channels, which enabled efficient electron and proton transport to the photocatalytic sites. As a result, the hydrogen production rate reached 4.78 mmol g −1 h −1 of H 2 O 2 over time, as illustrated in Figure 12a,b [72]. 

The synthesis of N-heterocyclic TpDz was done by conventional post-synthetic modification (PSM), while the synthesis of Py-OH-SaCOF was done by reticular chemical design. Unlike the conventional methods of incorporating specific functional groups into covalent organic frameworks, Quan et al. introduced a new enzyme-catalyzed PSM method, which entails a click reaction catalyzed by horseradish peroxidase (HRP).

Title: Catalyst Engineering for Photocatalytic Hydrogen Peroxide Production: State-of-the-Art Progress and Future Perspectives
Snippet: Another catalyst which is based on covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is trifluoro pyridyl TFPy COF. The presence of fluorinated pyridine moieties has been found to greatly improve the hydrophilicity of the material, which in turn improves the dispersion and availability of catalytic sites in aqueous media [76]. Covalent organic frameworks containing hydroquinone units (Tz-QH-COF) significantly improve the stability of photocatalysts in H 2 O 2 production [77]. Based on the success of C 3 N 4 materials, functional heptazine moieties have been combined with other functional units into ordered molecular frameworks to improve hydrogen peroxide production abilities [78]. The hydrogen peroxide production ability may also be affected by the heteroatom locking in COFs. For example, Nheteroatom-locked COFs have a photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production rate of 2.08 mmol g −1 h −1 in pure water and air. This is due to the 'locking' effect, which increases coplanarity and conjugation, and the 'heteroatom' effect, which increases the adsorption capacity of O 2 [79].

Title: Supercritical CO2-assisted rapid synthesis of covalent organic framework-based electrocatalyst for efficient two-electron oxygen reduction reaction
Snippet: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) hold significant promise as electrocatalysts, but their synthesis is typically constrained by prolonged reaction times (>72 h), high temperatures ( >120 °C), and the use of organic solvents. Conventional methods also involve multiple freeze-pump-thaw cycles, complicating scalability. Herein, we report a supercritical carbon dioxide (Sc-CO2)-assisted strategy for the rapid synthesis of COFs, enabling their direct in-situ growth on carbon substrates. This supercritical-solvothermal approach yields COF@CNT composites that exhibit effective electrocatalytic performance towards the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR). The resulting catalysts achieve a H2O2 production rate of 94 mol gcat−1 h−1 and a Faradaic efficiency exceeding 95% at 800 mA cm−2. By reducing the consumption of organic solvents, shortening reaction durations, and circumventing high temperatures, this method provides a scalable and efficient route for COF synthesis. Overall, the Sc-CO2 strategy provides a promising platform for the rapid development of COF-based electrocatalysts, combining enhanced efficiency, scalability, and environmental compatibility. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are attractive electrocatalysts, yet their synthesis is hindered by long reaction times, high temperatures, and the use of organic solvents. This works reports the use of supercritical CO2 to prepare efficient COF catalysts for the two electron oxygen reduction.

Title: Fully‐Conjugated Covalent Organic Frameworks with Two Metal Sites for Oxygen Electrocatalysis and Zn–Air Battery
Snippet: On the other hand, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) [21] possess an outstanding stable framework, constructed by covalent bonds, [22][23][24][25][26][27] but the non-metal frameworks also limit their electrocatalytic activity due to the lack of metal sites in the meantime. In order to break through this bottleneck, the metal-covalent organic frameworks (M-COFs), [28] constituted by the metal coordinated structure of MOFs and the covalent framework of COFs, have been considered as the "bridge" between MOFs and COFs, which should be a promising alternative for electrocatalysis. 

Similar to SACs, the metal sites in M-COFs are existed as single-metal sites, offering excellent catalytic activities toward electrocatalysis. [23] Recently, few M-COFs have been reported as catalysts for various electrochemical reactions (Figure 1a), such as porphyrin-, [29,30] bipyridine-, [31,32] and salen-based M-COFs. [33,34] However, the relatively low metal content and scanty metal site species in the existing M-COFs present a new challenge for further increasing the electrocatalytic activity. As far as known, the metal porphyrin-based M-COFs usually possess an excellent -conjugated structure, enabling the fast charge transfer in electrocatalytic reactions. [35] The metal sites in bipyridinebased M-COFs have highly unsaturation (M-N 2 moieties) and manifest a superior intrinsic activity. [32] Therefore, predictably, the combination between porphyrin and bipyridine subgroups could significantly increase the electrocatalytic activity by four advantages: 1) the bimetal active sites with high metal content and unsaturation; 2) two types of metal sites (M-N 2 and M-N 4 ) for synergistic catalysis, 3) the fully -conjugated structure with excellent conductivity for electron transfer, and 4) the expanded the porous structure for fast mass transfer.

Title: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) for electrochemical applications.
Snippet: Since the discovery of covalent organic frameworks in 2005 by Yaghi and co-workers, a series of COFs has been designed and synthesized targeting versatile applications. Given their controllable and well-defined structure, high porosity and surface area, COFs are promising materials for energy conversion and storage applications. Indeed, COFs feature certain advantages, which distinguish them from other typical materials used in this field. Compared to carbon-and graphene-based materials, there is at first very good structural control. By selection of appropriate linkage motifs and building blocks, materials with defined chemical structures, tuneable pore sizes and structures and low densities can be prepared, which are not seen in other typical carbon-based electrode materials. For example, metalcoordinating moieties in COFs can act as well-defined active sites for electrocatalysis or redox-active sites can enable an enhanced pseudocapacitive performance in supercapacitors or reversable processes in rechargeable batteries. On the other hand, the exclusive covalent connections can yield fully p-conjugated COFs enabling enhanced charge transport, which is often problematic in MOFs. 

To achieve high and robust electrocatalytic performance, increasing the number of active sites and intrinsic activity of each individual active site is required, which is enabled by the high surface area of COFs. Meanwhile, as the redox reactions in electrocatalysis generally happen between electrolyte and electrodes along with ion transport and electron exchange, novel synthetic approaches of COF-based electrocatalysts focus on facilitating mass transport and promoting the electric conductivity during electrocatalytic processes. The introduction of porous structures and conducting materials into COFs is thus a promising option to create more advanced electrocatalysts. 

In general, to design and fabricate efficient COF-based materials for electrochemical applications, different strategies have been developed, including: 

(i) Chemical modifications: depending on the desired application in electrocatalysis, COF structures can be controlled by developing different strategies including backbone modification, functional group modifications and post-synthetic modifications.

Title: Scalable Synthesis and Electrocatalytic Performance of Highly Fluorinated Covalent Organic Frameworks for Oxygen Reduction.
Snippet: In this study, we present a novel approach for the synthesis of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) that overcomes the common limitations of non-scalable solvothermal procedures. Our method allows for the room-temperature and scalable synthesis of a highly fluorinated DFTAPB-TFTA-COF, which exhibits intrinsic hydrophobicity. We used DFT-based calculations to elucidate the role of the fluorine atoms in enhancing the crystallinity of the material through corrugation effects, resulting in maximized interlayer interactions, as disclosed both from PXRD structural resolution and theoretical simulations. We further investigated the electrocatalytic properties of this material towards the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Our results show that the fluorinated COF produces hydrogen peroxide selectively with low overpotential (0.062 V) and high turnover frequency (0.0757 s-1) without the addition of any conductive additives. These values are among the best reported for non-pyrolyzed and metal-free electrocatalysts. Finally, we employed DFT-based calculations to analyse the reaction mechanism, highlighting the crucial role of the fluorine atom in the active site assembly. Our findings shed light on the potential of fluorinated COFs as promising electrocatalysts for the ORR, as well as their potential applications in other fields.

Title: Recent Advances of Covalent Organic Frameworks as Water Splitting Electrocatalysts
Snippet: Developing high performance, durable, yet low-lost catalyst for electrocatalytic water splitting technology has been a research priority to tackle the global energy crisis. In this regard, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have received numerous attentions as promising water splitting electrocatalysts as they can provide an excellent platform for settlement of electrocatalytic active site, high porosity, and good stability. In this review, recent advance on the design and application of COFs for water electrolysis, that are hydrogen and oxygen evolution reaction (HER and OER) electrocatalysts are briefly discussed. Among them, both noble and non-noble metals containing COFs as well as metal-free COFs based electrocatalysts are elaborated. Furthermore, a brief perspective on development of COFs in the field of water splitting electrocatalysis is provided.

snippet.text: In this study, we present a novel approach for the synthesis of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) that overcomes the common limitations of non-scalable solvothermal procedures. Our method allows for the room-temperature and scalable synthesis of a highly fluorinated DFTAPB-TFTA-COF, which exhibits intrinsic hydrophobicity. We used DFT-based calculations to elucidate the role of the fluorine atoms in enhancing the crystallinity of the material through corrugation effects, resulting in maximized interlayer interactions, as disclosed both from PXRD structural resolution and theoretical simulations. We further investigated the electrocatalytic properties of this material towards the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Our results show that the fluorinated COF produces hydrogen peroxide selectively with low overpotential (0.062 V) and high turnover frequency (0.0757 s-1) without the addition of any conductive additives. These values are among the best reported for non-pyrolyzed and metal-free electrocatalysts. Finally, we employed DFT-based calculations to analyse the reaction mechanism, highlighting the crucial role of the fluorine atom in the active site assembly. Our findings shed light on the potential of fluorinated COFs as promising electrocatalysts for the ORR, as well as their potential applications in other fields.

documents.snippet: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) hold significant promise as electrocatalysts, but their synthesis is typically constrained by prolonged reaction times (>72 h), high temperatures ( >120 °C), and the use of organic solvents. Conventional methods also involve multiple freeze-pump-thaw cycles, complicating scalability. Herein, we report a supercritical carbon dioxide (Sc-CO2)-assisted strategy for the rapid synthesis of COFs, enabling their direct in-situ growth on carbon substrates. This supercritical-solvothermal approach yields COF@CNT composites that exhibit effective electrocatalytic performance towards the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR). The resulting catalysts achieve a H2O2 production rate of 94 mol gcat−1 h−1 and a Faradaic efficiency exceeding 95% at 800 mA cm−2. By reducing the consumption of organic solvents, shortening reaction durations, and circumventing high temperatures, this method provides a scalable and efficient route for COF synthesis. Overall, the Sc-CO2 strategy provides a promising platform for the rapid development of COF-based electrocatalysts, combining enhanced efficiency, scalability, and environmental compatibility. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are attractive electrocatalysts, yet their synthesis is hindered by long reaction times, high temperatures, and the use of organic solvents. This works reports the use of supercritical CO2 to prepare efficient COF catalysts for the two electron oxygen reduction.

Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) were first developed in 2005. 9 COFs are a class of organic porous crystalline materials and are characterized by high surface area, high porosity, tunable pore size, and readily amenable surface properties. 7,8 Due to these exceptional features, COFs have been considered ideal materials for the development of membranes with high permselectivity. Snippet: Third, the development of new kinds of membranes with framework structures, such as covalent organic frameworks (COFs), which possess covalently linked topology, is of rapidly growing interest. Their ordered crystalline framework structures, inter-connective pores with controllable size and functionalization, as well as the framework tenability endow COFs with great potential in membrane separation. The transition from purely inorganic zeolite to inorganic-organic hybrid MOFs and then to purely organic COFs, reflects a new trend for the development of membrane materials. Also, the rigid covalent frameworks endow COF membranes with excellent tolerance and stability under harsh conditions, which may be helpful to anti-plasticization and anti-aging. There have been several reports about COF membranes in water treatment, pervaporation, hydrogen purification, and carbon capture. However, preparing defect-free COF membranes is still challenging, and currently, the pore size of COF membranes is often too large for ethylene/ethane and propylene/propane separation. Moreover, more control in fabricating COF membranes with appropriate pore size is needed for olefin/paraffin separations. 

Fourth, improving the membrane stability under actual conditions is an important consideration for practical adoption. High pressure feeds and impurities such as hydrogen sulfide, which is extremely harmful to the carriers of metal ions, are difficult challenges. Currently, there are few effective measures to protect carriers from poisoning; so simple and effective strategies are needed to inhibit the deactivation of metal ions. For the plasticization and aging resistance, hyper-crosslinking may possibly address this issue for polymeric membranes because it creates strong interchain interactions without sacrificing free volume. This strategy could also create more FFV to improve gas permeability. 

Fifth, developing large-scale fabrication methods for MOF membranes, especially with hollow fiber configuration, is crucial for industrial adoption. Hollow fiber membranes are possibly the most promising for commercial or practical application compared with other configurations because of the extremely high membrane areas, large productivity, and low footprint. Moreover, growing MOF layers on the bore side of hollow fibers is more attractive than the shell side because it is easier to maintain the mechanical robustness of the relatively fragile polycrystalline membrane during high density fiber packing into the modules.

Snippet: To objectively evaluate covalent organic framework membranes (COFMs), a comprehensive comparison was conducted between COFs and other common membrane materials -metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), hydrogenbonded organic frameworks (HOFs), polymers of intrinsic microporosity (PIMs), zeolites, traditional polymers, and layered 2D materials -focusing on pore structure, crystallinity, stability, diversity, designability, processing, key advantages, and limitations (Table 1). COFs feature highly ordered and tunable pores (typically 1 ~3 nm), enabling precise molecular sieving for selective separation of small molecules or ions. Their chemical versatility allows functional group modifications to enhance properties like hydrophilicity, antifouling, or target-specific interactions. COFMs also demonstrate superior stability in harsh environments (e.g., organic solvents, acids/ bases) compared to conventional polymers, making them suitable for diverse separation applications. However, challenges remain in green and scale-up preparation of defect-free COFMs. Additionally, pore alignment and intergrowth issues in thin-film configurations can compromise permeability and selectivity. While COFMs theoretically allow pore-size engineering, achieving sub-nanometer precision ( < 1 nm) for gas separation and ion sieving is difficult, limiting their competitiveness with other advanced membranes. Overall, COFMs show promise for high-precision separations but require breakthroughs in green and scalable fabrication, as well as sub-nanopore control, to bridge the gap between lab research and industrial adoption.

Title: Hydrogen-bonded organic framework@conductive metal-organic framework heterostructures for ampere-level hydrogen peroxide production
Snippet: Electrochemical two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e– ORR) in neutral environments holds remarkable promise for sustainable hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production. However, its practical application is largely hindered due to the scarcity of electrocatalysts with high selectivity and durability under ampere-level current densities. Herein, a hydrogen-bonded organic framework@conductive metal-organic framework (HOF@cMOF) heterostructure is designed for industrial-level H2O2 electrosynthesis. Through integrating DAT-HOF (DAT=diaminotriazole) and Co-cMOF, Co-N bonds formed at the heterointerface modulates the electronic structure of Co sites, optimizing the adsorption strength of oxygen intermediates with improved activity and selectivity. Besides, the formation of built-in electric field drives the proton migration from DAT-HOF to Co-cMOF, facilitating the O2 protonation to H2O2 at Co sites. In further combination with the high proton donation capability of DAT-HOF and high conductivity of Co-cMOF, efficient H2O2 production is achieved with a H2O2 Faradic efficiency of 97.1 ± 0.4%, a H2O2 yield of 738.9 mg h⁻1 cm⁻2 and a long-term durability over 100 h at 1200 mA cm⁻2. This work offers a high-performance electrocatalyst for promoting the industrial implementation of H2O2 electrosynthesis. Industrial-level electrochemical two-electron oxygen reduction reaction is promising for H2O2 production but lacks efficient catalysts. Here, the authors design a heterostructure catalyst for efficient H2O2 electrosynthesis at ampere-level current densities.

Title: Enhanced proton-feeding kinetics of metal-organic framework toward industrial-level H2O2 electrosynthesis for sustainable bleaching
Snippet: Eco-friendly electrocatalytic production of alkaline H2O2 via the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction offers a promising alternative to the conventional anthraquinone process, which is energy-intensive and poses explosion risks. Experiments and theoretical calculations elucidate that the electron-deficient Ni has accelerated water dissociation kinetics for proton-feeding to produce *OOH intermediate with suitable adsorption energy, boosting overall H2O2 electrosynthesis activity. Two-electron oxygen reduction reaction for hydrogen peroxide electrosynthesis is hindered by slow proton-feeding kinetics. Here, authors report bio-inspired B coordinated Ni-based metal-organic frameworks to accelerate water dissociation, achieving industrial-level hydrogen peroxide production.

Title: Unraveling Dimensional Tuning: From 2D to 3D in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Enhanced 2e– Oxygen Reduction Reaction
Snippet: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with a two-dimensional (2D) topology have recently emerged as promising catalyst systems for the electrosynthesis of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) from oxygen (O2). Title: Exploring Advanced Oxygen Reduction Reaction Electrocatalysts: The Potential of Metal-Free and Non-Pyrolyzed Covalent Organic Frameworks.

Snippet: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is a versatile and environmentally friendly oxidant with broad applications in industry, energy, and environmental remediation. Snippet: In this study, we present a novel approach for the synthesis of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) that overcomes the common limitations of non-scalable solvothermal procedures. Title: Hydrogen-bonded organic framework@conductive metal-organic framework heterostructures for ampere-level hydrogen peroxide production
Snippet: Electrochemical two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e– ORR) in neutral environments holds remarkable promise for sustainable hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production. Title: Enhanced proton-feeding kinetics of metal-organic framework toward industrial-level H2O2 electrosynthesis for sustainable bleaching
Snippet: Eco-friendly electrocatalytic production of alkaline H2O2 via the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction offers a promising alternative to the conventional anthraquinone process, which is energy-intensive and poses explosion risks. We propose that B-O-Ni motifs of B-NiBDC induce the formation of electron-deficient Ni active sites. Experiments and theoretical calculations elucidate that the electron-deficient Ni has accelerated water dissociation kinetics for proton-feeding to produce *OOH intermediate with suitable adsorption energy, boosting overall H2O2 electrosynthesis activity. Two-electron oxygen reduction reaction for hydrogen peroxide electrosynthesis is hindered by slow proton-feeding kinetics. Here, authors report bio-inspired B coordinated Ni-based metal-organic frameworks to accelerate water dissociation, achieving industrial-level hydrogen peroxide production.

However, designing 2D catalysts to achieve higher H2O2 selectivity presents a significant challenge because of the extensive layer stacking and the aggregated active sites located in the basal planes. It results in lower atom utilization, which requires attention. In this study, we present two functionally similar COFs: one with a 2D rhombus topology (2D@BT_TPA-COF) and another with a three-dimensional (3D) noninterpenetrated pts topology (3D@BT_TPA-COF). Both COFs were utilized for the 2e– oxygen reduction reaction (2e– ORR). Tunning the dimensionality from 2D to 3D resulted in an increase in H2O2 selectivity from approximately ∼56% to approximately ∼96% (at 0.4 V) and a rise in the turnover frequency (TOF) from 0.05 to 0.08 s–1 at 0.3 V. snippet.text: Eco-friendly electrocatalytic production of alkaline H2O2 via the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction offers a promising alternative to the conventional anthraquinone process, which is energy-intensive and poses explosion risks. However, the industrial adoption of this approach is hindered by sluggish proton-feeding kinetics of heterogeneous electrocatalysts, which restricts the achievable current densities. Herein, we develop Ni-based metal-organic frameworks with a bio-inspired B-coordination (B-NiBDC). The B-NiBDC shows Faradaic efficiency of ~90% for H2O2 electrosynthesis at 1000 mA cm−2, obtaining ~7.49 wt.% H2O2 alkaline solution for bleaching under urea oxidation-assisted energy-saving system. This has led to a significant increase in pulp brightness by 25-39 % (International Organization for Standardization, ISO). We propose that B-O-Ni motifs of B-NiBDC induce the formation of electron-deficient Ni active sites. Experiments and theoretical calculations elucidate that the electron-deficient Ni has accelerated water dissociation kinetics for proton-feeding to produce *OOH intermediate with suitable adsorption energy, boosting overall H2O2 electrosynthesis activity. Two-electron oxygen reduction reaction for hydrogen peroxide electrosynthesis is hindered by slow proton-feeding kinetics. Here, authors report bio-inspired B coordinated Ni-based metal-organic frameworks to accelerate water dissociation, achieving industrial-level hydrogen peroxide production.
